wisdom.title: Morning Wisdom
wisdom.text:
🌅 0600 Morning Wisdom
The Lord calls His sons to stand firm in the truth of His eternal Word, for He is the source of all order and strength.

📖 Scripture — Proverbs 8
Listen, for I speak of noble things, and my mouth opens in righteousness. For my mouth will utter truth, and wickedness is an abomination to my lips. All the words of my mouth are righteous; there is nothing twisted or crooked in them. They are all straight to him who understands, and right to those who find knowledge. Accept my instruction instead of silver, and knowledge rather than choice gold, for wisdom is better than jewels, and all that you may desire cannot compare with her. I, Wisdom, dwell with prudence, and I find knowledge and discretion. The fear of the LORD is hate of evil; pride and arrogance and the way of evil and perverted speech I hate. Counsel and sound knowledge are mine; I have understanding and strength. By me kings reign, and rulers decree what is just; by me rulers rule, and nobles, all who govern rightly. I love those who love me, and those who seek me diligently will find me. Riches and honor are with me, enduring wealth and righteousness. My fruit is better than gold, even fine gold, and my yield than choice silver. I walk in the way of righteousness, in the paths of justice, yielding an inheritance among those who love me, and filling their treasuries.

⸻

🧭 Context Summary
Solomon presents Wisdom as a divine personification calling out to the sons of men in the public squares. This passage establishes that true wisdom is not merely intellectual but is rooted in the fear of the LORD and results in righteous living. It stands in stark contrast to the foolishness that leads to destruction, offering instead a path of justice and enduring honor. The Lord desires His people to choose this higher treasure over the fleeting allure of material wealth.

⸻

🛡️ Reflection for a REAL MAN — Embraces Righteousness
Brother, you know that a ship is only as strong as its hull. In the same way, your life is only as stable as the foundation upon which you build it. The text declares that Wisdom speaks nothing twisted or crooked. For a man who has seen the chaos of war and the complexities of civilian life, this purity is not just a theological concept; it is a tactical necessity. You cannot navigate the storms of fatherhood and leadership if your compass is calibrated to the shifting sands of cultural compromise. You must anchor your heart in what is straight and true.

The Lord does not call you to be a soft man, but a wise one. Wisdom dwells with prudence and strength. These are not feminine virtues in the worldly sense; they are the bedrock of godly masculinity. To love Wisdom is to love the way the LORD has ordered His creation. It means you do not shy away from the hard truths of Scripture, even when the world calls them outdated. You embrace the role of headship not as a burden, but as a privilege granted by the Creator. You provide protection and provision because you understand that your family looks to you as a reflection of Christ’s love for the Church.

Do not seek the approval of men, brother. The text says that by Wisdom, kings reign and rulers decree justice. Your authority in your home and your community flows from your submission to God’s authority. When you walk in the way of righteousness, you do not do it for applause. You do it because you love the LORD and desire to honor Him. Your fruit is better than gold because it endures. In a world that values performance, your faithfulness to your covenant duties is your greatest testimony.

⸻

⛏️ Personal Application — Embraces Righteousness
• Read Proverbs 8 aloud at the start of each day to recalibrate your mind on God’s truth.
• Identify one area of your family leadership where you have compromised with cultural trends, and repent, returning to biblical headship.
• Teach your children the difference between worldly success and godly righteousness through concrete examples of your daily decisions.
• Pray for the courage to speak truth to your male peers, even when it is unpopular, modeling the fear of the LORD.

⸻

🙏 Prayer
Father, I thank You for the gift of Wisdom, which comes from You alone. Forgive me for the times I have sought the approval of men over the approval of You. Give me the strength to embrace Your righteousness in my role as husband and father. By the power of Your Holy Spirit, help me to walk in the paths of justice and to lead my household with prudence and love. Let my life bear fruit that honors Your name. In the name of Jesus Christ, my Lord and Commander, I pray. Amen.

⚓ Helm Command: Secure your compass to the Word, brother, and sail true.

first.title: First Watch — The Husband's Post
first.text:
🕖 0700 First Watch — The Husband's Post
Brother, begin this watch by examining the covenantal fidelity required of a man who leads his household under the authority of the King.

📖 Scripture — Judges 19

A certain Levite lived in a remote area of the hill country of Ephraim, who had taken as his wife a young woman from Bethlehem in Judah. She became angry with him and left him, returning to her father’s house in Bethlehem. After four months, her husband went to her to speak kindly to her and restore her affection, bringing along a servant and a donkey. When her father saw him, he welcomed him warmly and urged him to stay for three days. On the fourth day, they ate and drank together before the man rose early to depart, but his father-in-law pressed him to stay another day. On the fifth day, the father-in-law urged him to linger until the afternoon, and they shared a meal again before the Levite prepared to leave with his two donkeys and his concubine. As they approached Jebus, which is Jerusalem, the servant advised his master to turn aside into the city of the Jebusites to spend the night, but the Levite refused, insisting on continuing to Gibeah of Benjamin where he could find lodging among his kinsmen. They stopped at Gibeah as the sun was setting, and no one offered them shelter until an old man from the hill country of Ephraim, who was residing there, took them into his home. While they were eating, men of the city, worthless fellows, surrounded the house and demanded that the host bring out the visitor so they could abuse him. The host went out to them and pleaded with them not to commit such a wicked act, offering his own daughter and the Levite’s concubine instead, but the men refused and forced the Levite out. The Levine took his concubine and pushed her out the door, and she lay at the entrance until morning. At dawn, she collapsed at the threshold, and when her husband came to open the door, he found her fallen with her hands at the entrance. He forced her onto his donkey and departed for home. When he arrived, he took a knife, cut his wife into twelve pieces, and sent the parts throughout the territory of Israel. Everyone who saw it said, “Never such a thing has been seen or done, from the day the people came up from the land of Egypt until this day. Consider it, take counsel, and speak up.”

⸻

🗺️ Briefing Summary
This passage depicts the horrific moral collapse of Israel during the period of the judges, a time when "everyone did what was right in his own eyes." The narrative serves as a grim warning against the consequences of spiritual apostasy and the breakdown of social and covenantal order. It highlights the vulnerability of the weak when the strong fail to uphold justice and hospitality. For the husband, it illustrates the catastrophic results of neglecting the sacred trust of protecting and valuing one’s wife.

⸻

❤️ Reflection for Your Wife — H.A.P.P.Y. Husband — Protecting

Brother, look closely at the Levite in this text. He is a man of God, a priest of the tribe of Levi, yet he fails miserably in his duty to protect his wife. He leaves her at the mercy of vile men to avoid personal risk or inconvenience. He prioritizes his own safety and comfort over the sanctity of the woman God has joined to him. This is not leadership; this is cowardice disguised as pragmatism.

As a husband to Maria, you are called to be her shield. Your headship is not a license for tyranny, nor is it an excuse for absenteeism. It is a burden of responsibility. You must stand between her and the chaos of a fallen world. When the night grows dark and the threats are real, you do not push her out the door. You do not offer her up to satisfy the demands of the wicked. You hold the line.

Your protection is both physical and spiritual. It means ensuring your home is a fortress of righteousness where fear has no place. It means speaking up for her when others would silence her. It means valuing her life above your own ease. The Levite’s failure led to death and division; your faithfulness leads to life and peace. Guard her heart and her body with the zeal of a man who knows he will give an account to the LORD for the stewardship of His gift.

⸻

⛏️ Personal Application — Protecting

• Conduct a weekly security audit of your home and vehicle, ensuring Maria feels physically safe in your care.
• Memorize Psalm 91 and pray it aloud over Maria each evening, declaring the LORD’s protection upon her.
• When Maria faces harassment or injustice, intervene immediately and decisively, refusing to remain silent.
• Teach your children to respect Maria’s authority and safety, modeling the protective headship you exercise.

🙏 Prayer from the Stateroom
Father, I confess that I often fear man more than I fear You. Forgive me for the times I have been passive when I should have been proactive, and selfish when I should have been sacrificial. Grant me the courage of a soldier and the tenderness of a husband. By the power of Your Holy Spirit, strengthen my arms to defend Maria and my heart to cherish her as Christ cherishes the Church. Give me discernment to recognize threats to her holiness and wisdom to meet them with righteous authority. In the name of Jesus Christ, my Lord and Commander, I commit this watch to You. Amen.

⚓ Helm Command: Brother, when your wife’s father calls you to her, do not let the comfort of your own roof or the fear of your own safety silence your duty to rescue her.

second.title: Second Watch — The Father's Charge
second.text:
🕚 1100 Second Watch — The Father's Charge

The assembly of Israel stands united in judgment, yet the path to obedience is paved with the sobering reality of human failure without divine grace.

📖 Scripture — Judges 20:1-25

All the men of Israel were gathered against the city, united as one man. The people counted themselves, one hundred and twenty thousand swordsmen, and seven hundred chosen men of all the people. Among all this people there were seven hundred chosen men left-handed, every one could sling a stone at a hair and not miss. Of all the people of Benjamin, twenty-six thousand swordsmen, besides all the men of Gibeah who numbered eight hundred chosen men. All these were men of war, every one fitted for the battle. Then the people went up to the house of God and inquired of the LORD. The children of Israel said, Who shall go up first for us against the children of Benjamin to battle? And the LORD said, Judah shall go up first. So the children of Israel rose up in the morning and encamped against Gibeah. The men of Israel went out against the people of Benjamin on the second day and drew up against them in battle at Gibeah. The men of Benjamin came out against them from Gibeah on that day and struck down four thousand and twenty men of Israel. Then the men of Israel encouraged themselves and again drew up in battle in the place where they had drawn up on the first day. And the children of Israel went up and wept before the LORD until the evening and inquired of the LORD. They said, Shall we again draw near to battle against the children of our brother Benjamin? And the LORD said, Go up against them. So the men of Israel came near against the children of Benjamin on the third day and drew up against Gibeah as at other times. And the children of Benjamin came out against them from Gibeah on the third day and struck down again some thirty-two thousand of the people of Israel. And they encouraged themselves and drew up in battle again in the place where they drew up on the second day. When the children of Israel had withdrawn themselves from the men of Benjamin, they said, Let us flee into our cities which are in the land. And all the people rose up as one man against the city. And the chosen men of Israel hid themselves in the ambush of the fields of Gibeah. And when the men of Israel gave way to the men of Benjamin, they began to strike down some of the people, as at the first time, and the men of Benjamin said, They are defeated before us as at the first time. But the men of Israel said, Let us flee into the plain and draw them from the city to the highways. And all the men of Israel rose up from their places and drew up against Gibeah on the fourth day. And the men of Israel went down before the men of Benjamin, and the men of Benjamin came out against them from Gibeah and struck down as at other times about thirty men of the people in the highways, one of which goes up to the house of God, and the other goes down to the plain. Then the men of Israel said, We will flee before them as at the first time, and we will draw them out from the city to the highways. And all the men of Israel rose up against Gibeah on the fifth day and drew up against it. And the chosen men of Israel came out of their ambush and rushed on Gibeah. And they fought with them, and the men of Benjamin began to be struck down before the men of Israel. And the men of Israel withdrew themselves because of the men of Benjamin, for they said, We flee before them as in the former battles. Then all the men of Israel made a retreat from the men of Benjamin, for the men of Benjamin said, They are defeated before us as in the former battles. But the men of Israel said, Let us flee before them into the plain, and let us bring them out from the city to the highways. And when the men of Benjamin had begun to be struck down and the men of Israel said, We flee before them into the plain, behold, all Gibeah was on fire, the smoke of the city went up to heaven. Then the men of Israel turned in the battle, and the men of Benjamin were terrified, for they saw that disaster was upon them. Therefore they turned their backs before the men of Israel in the way of the wilderness, but the battle overtook them. And those who came out of the cities destroyed them in the midst of them. They surrounded the men of Benjamin, chased them, and trampled them down easily in the vicinity of Gibeah on the east. Eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell, all mighty men of valor. But they fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, and they gleaned of them five thousand men on the highways. And they pressed hard after them as far as Gidom and struck down two thousand men of them. So the men of Israel turned back against the men of Benjamin, and struck them with the edge of the sword, from man even to beast, and all the cities that were found, and all the inhabitants of the cities they put to the sword.

⸻

🗺️ Field Notes
The children of Israel gathered to seek the LORD’s will before engaging in a civil war that would devastate the tribe of Benjamin. Though they sought His guidance, their initial reliance on military strength without true repentance led to costly defeats. It was only when they followed the LORD’s specific tactical instruction and executed judgment with covenantal severity that victory was secured.

⸻

👨‍👧 Reflection for Your Children — F.U.L.F.I.L.L.E.D. Father — Disciplining

Brother, look to the gravity of Judges 20 to understand the weight of paternal authority. God does not treat sin lightly, and neither should a father who seeks to lead his house in truth. When Gideon is nineteen and beginning to understand the world, teach him that discipline is not anger, but a holy separation from evil. Boaz at fourteen is old enough to see that justice requires courage, not just comfort. Young Shiloh must learn early that the rod of correction is a tool of love, meant to guide him away from the destruction that sin brings.

You must be the spiritual captain in your home, brother. Your duty is to protect your family from the corruption of this age by establishing clear, firm boundaries rooted in Scripture. Do not fear being seen as harsh by the world; fear the judgment of God who commands you to train up your children in the way they should go. Your authority is a stewardship from the LORD, and you will give an account for how you wield it.

Gideon needs to see that his father’s discipline is consistent with God’s Word, not his own mood. Boaz needs to understand that submission to godly authority is a virtue, not a weakness. Shiloh needs the security of knowing that his father’s rules are designed to keep him safe from the consequences of his own folly. This is the burden of the patriarch, brother. You lead, you protect, and you correct with the seriousness of a man who fears God more than men.

⸻

⛏️ Personal Application — Disciplining
• Establish a clear, written code of conduct for your household that aligns with the 1689 London Baptist Confession of Faith.
• Enforce immediate and consistent consequences for disobedience, ensuring Gideon understands the seriousness of truthfulness.
• Use Boaz’s growing maturity to instruct him in the principles of justice and the necessity of repentance.
• Guide Shiloh’s early years with gentle but firm correction, establishing the habit of obedience before the age of reason fully sets in.

🙏 Prayer from the Wardroom
Father, we come before Your throne of grace, acknowledging our need for Your sovereign guidance in the duties of fatherhood. Grant us the wisdom to lead our households with the same seriousness You displayed in Your judgment, that we might raise up a seed that honors You. By the power of Your Holy Spirit, give us the courage to discipline with love and the humility to submit to Your Word in all things. Strengthen our hands to protect our families from the snares of the enemy, and keep our hearts fixed on Your glory. In the name of Jesus Christ, my Lord and Commander, we pray. Amen.

⚓ Rudder Steer: Brother, steel your resolve to confront the entrenched corruption of your house with the relentless discipline of the twelve tribes.

third.title: Third Watch — The Citizen's Stand
third.text:
🕒 1500 Third Watch — The Citizen's Stand

Brother, stand firm in the covenant of your household while the world around you fractures under the weight of its own sin.

📖 Scripture — Judges 20:26-48

Then the children of Israel went up, and came up to the house of God, and remained there before the LORD until even, they lifted up their voices, and wept sore; And offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD, and sat there before the LORD, and ate and drank on that day sore, for they were in great heaviness for the people of Benjamin their brethren. And the children of Israel enquired of the LORD (and the days were past, and the ark of the covenant of God was there in those days, and Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, stood before it in those days) saying, Shall I go up any more to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother? or shall I cease? And the LORD said, Go up; for tomorrow will I deliver them into thine hand. And Israel came near against Benjamin the second day. And Benjamin went forth out of Gibeah against them the second day on the morrow, and destroyed down to the ground of Israel again eighteen thousand men. And the children of Israel, and the people, went up, and came to the house of God, and enquired of the LORD in the morning, saying, Who shall go up first for us to battle against the children of Benjamin? And the LORD said, Judah shall go up first. And the children of Israel drew near against the children of Benjamin the third day, and went to and fro until thou hadst given them into thine hand. And the children of Israel said, We are come near unto the children of Benjamin our brother. Now the men of Israel said, Let us flee, and bring them into the wilderness as before. And the children of Benjamin said to themselves, They are come near against us as at the first: but let us slay of them, even as before, in the highways, one of them up on one side, and another on the other side, till we have consumed them. And when the children of Benjamin were begun to be smitten, and the men of Israel said, We be smitten before them as at the first: but let us flee after them in the highway, and bring them unto the wilderness. And it came to pass, when the men of Israel fled in the presence of Benjamin in the highway, that they cast themselves down by the side of the wilderness; but all that came to Gibeah were slain of them; and there fell of Israel about thirty men of foot; for they said, We will flee before them in the highway, as at the first. And the men of Israel said, If we flee before them in the highway, which they go up to Bethel, we will set an ambush in the cities in the vineyards. And the men of Israel went up against the children of Benjamin on the third day, and went up toward Gibeah, and laid war against it as at other times. And the men of Israel set an ambush round about against Gibeah. And the men of Israel went up against the children of Benjamin; and the men of Israel said unto them, Let us flee, I pray you, as at other times, and let us bring them out from the cities in the highways. And it came to pass, when they had drawn them out of the cities, that all the people rose up against them, and the ambush broke forth out of its place, and smote the children of Benjamin; and they saw, and, behold, the smoke of the city ascended up to heaven. And when the men of Israel turned again in the battle, Benjamin began to smite and slay of the men of Israel, and there fell down of Israel in all the people about thirty thousand men. And the battle was very sore; and the men of Israel gave back, because they trusted unto the ambush which they had set against Gibeah. And the men of Israel fled in the presence of the children of Benjamin; and the children of Benjamin said, Smite them down, as at the first. But the men of Israel said, Let us flee in the wilderness. Now there was an ambush hastened against Gibeah on every side, and the ambush smote all the city with the edge of the sword. And the appointed sign between the men of Israel and the ambush was, that when they made a great smoke with fire should rise up of the city. And Benjamin began to smite and slay of the men of Israel about thirty persons: for they said, Surely they are smitten down before us, as in the first battle. But when the men of Israel began to flee, they cried out after Benjamin; and the men of Israel smote the Rutites, and slew all the men of the city with the edge of the sword. And there was an ambush that hastened from their place, even from the place of the ambush, from the plain toward Gibeah, and smote it with the edge of the sword. And the appointed sign, that they made haste to the wilderness, and spread themselves along by the side of the cities. And all the people returned against the children of Benjamin; and the battle was sore; and I sent out the men of Gibeah, and the children of Benjamin were aware of it. And the men of Israel went back against the children of Benjamin on the fourth day; and Israel fought against Benjamin from morning until the evening, and he prevailed against Benjamin. And the men of Israel went up against the children of Benjamin, and smote them with the edge of the sword, and the inhabitant of every city, and the cattle, and all that they found, and all the cities which they found they set on fire. So the men of Israel destroyed all the cities among the children of Benjamin, the inhabitants of the cities, and the cattle, and all that they found, and all the cities which they found they set on fire. And all the people, every man of them, turned again unto his house and to his inheritance; neither went they out to the brethren again.

⸻

🛰️ Situation Report
The tribe of Benjamin, having abandoned the moral laws of God, finds itself isolated and defeated despite its military strength. The nation of Israel, though initially hesitant and spiritually confused, ultimately submits to the Lord’s judgment and executes a decisive victory. This passage illustrates the terrible cost of sin and the necessity of national repentance to restore covenant order.

⸻

🛡️ Reflection for a R.E.S.O.L.U.T.E. Citizen — Steadfast

Fredericksburg (local)
Brother, look to the ground beneath your boots. The battle at Fredericksburg was a grim testament to the futility of charging against fortified sin without divine favor. The men who stood on Marye’s Heights did not fight for a noble cause, but for a fractured union, and the result was a slaughter of brothers. You must be steadfast not merely in your stance, but in your alignment with the Right. When the enemy charges, do not move in panic. Stand your ground in prayer and in the truth, knowing that your defense is not in the strength of your armor, but in the righteousness of your Cause.

Virginia (state)
The Commonwealth of Virginia has a history of defining itself through resistance, often against the very Providence that established it. Yet, the true steadfastness of this land is found in its founding fathers who looked to the Scriptures for their civil order. They understood that a state cannot stand if its foundations are rotten with moral compromise. As a citizen of this state, you are called to uphold the laws that protect the family and the church. Do not waver when the culture demands you abandon traditional roles. Your steadfastness is a witness to the local community, showing that a man who fears God is not easily moved by the winds of public opinion.

United States (nation)
The United States was founded on the principle that all men are created equal under the Law of God. When the nation strays from this foundation, it invites the very judgment described in Judges. The civil authority is ordained by God to punish evil and praise those who do good. A man who is steadfast respects this authority, not because he is a slave to the state, but because he is a servant of the King. When the nation is in turmoil, the steadfast citizen does not join the mob. He holds the line of truth, supports his neighbors, and trusts that the Lord is still on the throne, even when the institutions of man seem to crumble.

⸻

⛏️ Personal Application — Steadfast
• Review your family’s spiritual schedule for the next week and ensure that Scripture reading is non-negotiable, regardless of work demands.
• Identify one area where you have compromised your moral convictions for the sake of convenience, and repent of it this evening.
• Speak to your children about the duty of a man to protect his home, using a specific example of your own steadfastness in a recent conflict.
• Visit a neighbor who is struggling with faith or duty, and offer practical help and prayer, demonstrating the strength of the covenant community.

🦅 This Day in American History — April 8
On April 8, 1864, after long and bitter debate, the United States Senate passed the Thirteenth Amendment to abolish slavery throughout the land, a great labor of conscience that would not be fully ratified for another year and more. On the same day in 1913, the Seventeenth Amendment was completed when Connecticut cast the deciding vote, giving the people the direct choice of their senators. A Steadfast citizen takes heart that the slow and costly work of perfecting self-government goes forward year upon year, and he lends his own patient hand to it, knowing that God honors those who persevere in the labor of justice and ordered liberty.

🙏 Prayer from the Bridge
Father, I thank You for the example of Your people who stood firm when the world fell away. Forgive me for my timidity and my compromise. Give me the grace to be a steadfast husband, a faithful father, and a loyal citizen. By the power of Your Holy Spirit, strengthen my will to obey Your commands, even when they are costly. Guard my heart against the fear of man, and anchor my soul in the certainty of Your promises. In the name of Jesus Christ, my Lord and Commander, I pray. Amen.

⚓ Rudder Steer: Brother, cease the futile charge and descend to the house of God to weep with your voice and feast on the peace offerings until the evening shadows fall.

peace.title: Evening Peace
peace.text:
🌙 2100 Evening Peace

Rest your weary mind under the canopy of Zion’s eternal security.

📖 Scripture — Psalm 87

Of Zion it shall be said,
This one and that one were born in her,
and the Most High Himself established her.
The LORD records in the register of the peoples,
“This one was born there.”
Selah
And of Zion it shall be said,
“Who can recount all that she has done?”
For the Maker of her will make her remembered.
When He makes the peoples sing,
He will say, “This one was born there.”
Selah
The BLIND shall receive their sight,
and the lame shall leap like a deer;
then the word of the LORD shall be established.
The LORD has made known His salvation;
He has revealed His righteousness in the sight of the nations.
He has remembered His mercy and faithfulness
to the house of Israel.
All the ends of the earth have seen
the salvation of our God.

⸻

🌾 Reflection for a Man at Home and in Community

As a HAPPY husband, you recognize that your home is a small reflection of Zion’s peace, established not by your own strength but by the Most High Himself. You do not strive to create a perfect environment through sheer willpower, for you know that the LORD records the deeds of your household in His eternal register. Your joy flows from the assurance that your wife and children are held in the hands of a Sovereign God who desires to make His salvation known even within the four walls of your dwelling.

As a FULFILLED father, you teach your children that their ultimate citizenship is not of this world but of Zion, where every righteous lineage is accounted for by grace. You point them away from the shifting sands of cultural approval and toward the solid rock of Christ, who alone can recount all that God has done in their lives. Your instruction is grounded in the reality that the LORD has made known His salvation, and you have the privilege of introducing your offspring to the Maker who established their spiritual birth.

As a RESOLUTE citizen, you stand firm in the knowledge that the LORD has revealed His righteousness in the sight of all nations, and your duty is to walk humbly in that light. You do not fear the opposition of the age, for the God who makes the lame leap and the blind see is the same God who sustains your resolve. You serve your community with clarity and strength, knowing that your labor in the Lord is not in vain, and that the ends of the earth are called to witness the salvation of your God.

🙏 Prayer from the Stateroom

Father, we thank You for the peace of Zion that anchors our souls. By the power of Your Holy Spirit, strengthen us to lead our homes with wisdom and courage, that our households may reflect Your glory. Keep us steadfast in our covenant duties, that we may stand resolute as citizens of Your kingdom. In the name of Jesus Christ, my Lord and Commander, we pray. Amen.

⚓ Rudder Steer: Anchor your heart in Zion’s stability and lead your household with quiet confidence.
